INFORMATION

COMMON INQUIRIES

I work across product design, brand identity, and visual systems — from early-stage startups building their first app to established companies looking to sharpen how they show up in the world. If there's a real problem to solve and intention behind the work, I'm interested.

Every project starts with discovery — understanding your audience, your goals, and the gap between where you are and where you want to be. From there I move through strategy, concept, and execution, but it's never a rigid waterfall. Good design is iterative, and I stay close to the work at every stage.

Both. I've worked with founders on day one and with teams that have been around for decades. The stage matters less than the clarity of intent. If you know what you're trying to build — even roughly — we can work from there.

It depends on scope. A focused brand identity usually runs four to six weeks. A full product design engagement can span several months. I'd rather give you an honest timeline upfront than rush something that needs room to breathe.

Mostly: context, candor, and a willingness to push past the obvious. The best briefs aren't necessarily the most detailed — they're the most honest. Tell me what you're building, who it's for, and what success looks like. We'll figure out the rest together.

item.title: MOLESKIN
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
MOLESKIN

client: Moleskine S.r.l.
role: Lead Product Designer
industry: Stationery / Design Tools
year: 2024
services: Product Design, Structural Engineering Liaison, Concept Direction, Limited Edition Development
deliverables: Product form specification, material & binding research report, packaging concept, production handoff documentation

Moleskine approached this as a limited-edition collaboration: a notebook designed for architects, with physical features that reflect how architects actually work. I introduced a dual-cover system — hard outer shell, soft inner — that allows the book to lie flat under pressure, a feature obsessively requested by the profession.

Grid and line pages were co-developed with practicing architects to refine ruling dimensions. The edition sold out in three weeks and became the basis for Moleskine's broader professional series.

item.title: GRACIOUS OM
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
GRACIOUS OM

client: Gracious Om Wellness
role: Brand Identity Designer
industry: Wellness / Lifestyle
year: 2022
services: Brand Identity, Logo Design, Visual System, Packaging Application, Brand Guidelines
deliverables: Primary & secondary logo suite, color palette, typography system, packaging design (3 SKUs), brand guidelines document

Gracious Om is a wellness brand rooted in Ayurvedic tradition, launched by a founder who wanted the brand to feel ancient without feeling costume. The identity needed to carry spiritual weight and work on a soap bar, a candle, a tote bag, and a website simultaneously.

I built a mark from a geometric interpretation of the Om symbol — stripped of ornamentation, locked into a grid — paired with a serif wordmark that reads like it's been around for decades. Every touchpoint was designed to feel like it was handed down, not launched.

item.title: SELTZER SODA
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
SELTZER SODA

client: Seltzer Beverages Co.
role: Graphic Designer
industry: Food & Beverage
year: 2024
services: Packaging Design, Brand Visual Language, Typography, Color System Design
deliverables: Can design across 5 flavor variants, brand style guide excerpt, retail mockups, digital asset kit

Seltzer needed to compete on a shelf that had become a visual arms race of bright colors and aggressive typography. Rather than shout louder, I took the opposite approach: restraint as a differentiator.

A muted palette inspired by mineral water geology, a wordmark set in a condensed grotesque at confident scale, and flavor cues expressed through subtle gradient fields rather than illustrated fruit. On a shelf full of noise, Seltzer became the one you notice by not trying.

item.title: WELEDA
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
WELEDA

client: Weleda AG
role: Senior Product Designer
industry: Natural Beauty / Pharmaceutical
year: 2023
services: Product Design, Ergonomic Research, Sustainable Material Consultation, Form Development
deliverables: Revised 3D product form, material specification report, manufacturing liaison documentation, production prototype direction

Weleda asked a pointed question: what does a 100-year-old brand look like when it's held in your hand? Their iconic cream needed a new vessel — one that honored the brand's heritage while meeting the ergonomic and sustainability standards of a modern consumer.

I redesigned the tube form to reduce material waste by 18%, improved the dispensing mechanism for single-handed use, and refined the cap proportions to echo the brand's botanical identity. Old values, new form.

item.title: LARYSSA SOAP
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
LARYSSA SOAP

client: Laryssa Skincare
role: Graphic Designer & Art Director
industry: Beauty / Personal Care
year: 2022
services: Packaging Design, Typography, Art Direction, Print Production Oversight
deliverables: Label design across 6 SKUs, brand color system, print-ready files, mockup library for e-commerce

Laryssa is a small-batch soap brand built around ritual — the idea that the objects we touch every morning should feel like they belong there. The packaging brief was deceptively simple: premium, minimal, feminine without being precious.

I developed a label system using a single typeface in two weights, an earthy ink palette pulled from the soap's natural colorways, and a layout that reads beautifully both on a shelf and in a flat lay. The result is packaging that earns its place in a well-considered bathroom.

item.title: ROMBO PICK
item.dc:creator: MikulasKarpeta
item.content:encoded:
ROMBO PICK

client: Rombo Instruments
role: Lead Product Designer
industry: Music / Consumer Goods
year: 2026
services: Product Design, Industrial Form Development, Material Specification,
Prototype Direction
deliverables: Concept sketches, 3D CAD models, material & finish specification, production-ready technical drawings

The guitar pick is one of the most overlooked objects in music — used thousands of times a day, almost never designed with intention. Rombo came to me with a simple challenge: make something a musician would actually want to hold.

The result was a precision-molded pick with an asymmetric grip ridge, calibrated bevel angles for different playing styles, and a material composite that balances rigidity with tactile warmth. It looks like a pick. It performs like an instrument.
